record.paper_title: Stationary solutions of the axially symmetric Einstein-Vlasov system: present status and open problems
record.context_brief: Self-gravitating Vlasov matter around central black holes
record.original_question: Can one find general axially symmetric self-gravitating stationary Einstein-Vlasov solutions with a central black hole, beyond perturbative constructions near Kerr in which the Vlasov matter is small or close to vacuum, for example by adapting the existing numerical code to impose inner boundary conditions at the black-hole horizon?

evidence.quote: An interesting direction in which to extend the study of regular axisymmetric stationary solutions of the Einstein-Vlasov system, is to consider solutions with a central black hole. This imposes inner boundary conditions at the black hole horizon.

By the nature of the proof however, the matter must be small (close to vacuum), and it remains an open problem to find general axially symmetric self-gravitating solutions of the Einstein-Vlasov system with a central black hole.
A sensible starting place is to probe this problem numerically. One approach would be to modify the code used in [2, 3] and documented in [6].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Einstein–Vlasov system in four spacetime dimensions, in which the spacetime metric g on a Lorentzian manifold M is coupled to a non-negative phase-space distribution function f on the mass-shell {(x,p) ∈ TM : g(p,p) = -1, p future-directed} via

  Ric(g) - (1/2) R(g) g = 8π T[f],   T_{μν}[f](x) = ∫ f(x,p) p_μ p_ν dvol_p,

while f satisfies the Vlasov (collisionless transport) equation along the geodesic flow on the mass shell.

Seek stationary, axially symmetric solutions (g, f) admitting two commuting Killing vector fields, one timelike at infinity and one spacelike with closed orbits, such that the spacetime is asymptotically flat and contains a central black hole, i.e. there is a non-trivial event horizon H whose induced geometry one prescribes as an inner boundary, and such that f is supported in the domain of outer communications and is not required to be small (in particular, not a perturbation of a vacuum Kerr solution).

Question: Do there exist such stationary axially symmetric self-gravitating Einstein–Vlasov solutions with a central black hole in a genuinely non-perturbative regime (the Vlasov matter not assumed close to vacuum)? Equivalently, can one construct such solutions—analytically or numerically (e.g. by imposing inner boundary conditions at the horizon in an iterative scheme)—beyond the known perturbative existence near Kerr with small matter content?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent surveys on stationary axisymmetric Einstein–Vlasov solutions state that the only existence result with a central black hole is Jabiri's perturbative construction near Kerr, requiring small (near-vacuum) Vlasov matter; constructing general (non-perturbative) self-gravitating axially symmetric stationary solutions with a central black hole remains explicitly listed as an open problem, and no published numerical or analytical solution in this regime has been found.

status_evidence.title: Stationary solutions of the axially symmetric Einstein-Vlasov system: present status and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Jabiri proved existence by perturbation about Kerr; matter must be small. It remains an open problem to find general axially symmetric self-gravitating solutions of the Einstein-Vlasov system with a central black hole.
status_evidence.claim: The non-perturbative existence problem with a central black hole is explicitly open.

status_evidence.title: Stationary solutions of the Einstein-Vlasov system (thesis)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses perturbative existence of axisymmetric stationary Einstein-Vlasov solutions around Kerr black holes.
status_evidence.claim: Existing rigorous black-hole results are perturbative around Kerr.
